title: Fix: the 32nd block
hints: Blocks 0–30 are fine; the trouble starts at block 31 (and again at 63). What is special about bit 31 of a 32-bit word?

`1` is an `int`, so `1 << (block % WORD_BITS)` is computed in **signed** 32-bit arithmetic. Shifting a 1 into the sign bit (`1 << 31`) can't be represented in an `int`, which is undefined behaviour, even though the result is then converted to `uint32_t`.
Make the 1 unsigned and 32 bits wide before shifting: `return UINT32_C(1) << (block % WORD_BITS);` (or `(uint32_t)1 << ...`).
